krait.etym: Borrowed from Hindi करैत (karait), possibly from Kurux, a Dravidian language.

g: Any of several brightly-coloured, venomous snakes, of the genus Bungarus, of southeast Asia.
x: On visiting the General Hospital, on the morning of the 22nd of August, I was informed that one of the punkah coolies had been bitten about 8.30 p.m., the night before, by a krait, whose venom is virulently poisonous.
Now, if you run into one of these kraits, you better NOT run away else you're a goner. It'll catch you for sure and you will die in your tracks.
Very much in my thoughts is Joe Slowinski, a herpetologist killed a few years earlier by a misidentified juvenile krait, a snake so small that he couldn't tell if the fang had punctured the skin.

krypton.etym: From Ancient Greek κρυπτός (kruptós, “hidden”) + -on, used for all noble gases.

g: The chemical element (symbol Kr) with an atomic number of 36. It is a colourless, odourless noble gas that only reacts with fluorine. It is one of the rarest gases in the Earth's atmosphere.
